To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the kinematic approximation of the momentum equation is not sufficient to simulate the propagation of debris flows, and that the inclusion of diffusion processes in the model can significantly improve the prediction of the flow evolution.

(i) the application of a kinematic model to a real case scenario of debris flow propagation can lead to a good approximation of the flow dynamics, but (ii) the kinematic model is unable to predict the spreading of the flow wave, which can only be described with a more general model, such as the diffusion wave model.
kinematic models can be used to predict the flow velocity, the flow depth and the flow thickness of debris flows, but not the flow width.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the application of the kinematic models to the simulation of debris flows.
the identification of the effective value of a diffusion coefficient in a kinematic model for the simulation of debris flows.
the application of kinematics models to simulate debris flows and with the identification of the effective values of neglected terms in the model.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the diffusion processes are negligible for debris flows, and the kinematic approximation can be used to simulate the debris flow propagation, provided that the flow is not affected by the diffusion processes.
, in the absence of diffusion processes, the kinematic approximation can be successfully applied for the prediction of debris flows.
the kinematic approximation can be successfully applied to simulate the debris flow propagation along a steep torrent, provided that the diffusion process is neglected.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in order to obtain a good agreement with the field observations, the kinematic model must be coupled with an empirical diffusion wave model.
, although the kinematic approximation is not able to reproduce the diffusion process of debris flows, its results are still acceptable when the diffusion term is not significant.

, although kinematic models are able to predict well the propagation of debris flows, their application to simulate diffusive processes is questionable, since they neglect the diffusion term in the momentum equation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, even though the kinematic approximation is a good first-order approximation for debris flows, the neglected terms in this approximation can not be considered negligible and must be taken into account in the modelling process.

, in the case of a debris flow with low Froude number, kinematic models can be successfully employed to predict the propagation of debris flows, even if the diffusive processes are not taken into account.
, even if the application of a diffusion model is more complex than that of a kinematic model, it is necessary to use it in order to simulate debris flow dynamics in real mountain torrents.
